name: The Pullman household at 1729 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_pullman_mrs_george_m

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1729 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1729 Mrs. Geo. M. Pullman; Miss R. S. Robinson.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1729, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The three live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. A coachman's wife and children in the rear building are named in his note rather than carded. The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Mrs. George M. Pullman
persons.note: The 1900 census lists G. M. Pullman here as head, with the personal columns written 'Unknown' (ED 40, sheet 1A, line 1, leaf n794).

persons.name: Miss R. S. Robinson
persons.note: First listed at 1729 in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904); the 1904 edition does not list her, so whether she lived here on 1 July 1904 is not documented. What she was to Mrs. Pullman (relative, companion or secretary) is not printed.

persons.name: Emma Scott

born.note: The census gives October 1870, age 30 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Housekeeper" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a servant (housekeeper); born October 1870 (the figures are hard to read), in England, came to the United States in 1880, single. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the dwelling the enumerator visited next, which has no number of its own and follows 1729, as the head of his own household there (coachman); born March 1854, in Germany, came to the United States in 1885, married.
